question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼\frac{3}{2}-\frac{14}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi x}{6}).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=-3,$ we have

$$
sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi (-3)}{6})=sin\,(\frac{\pi }{2}-n\pi )=(-1)^{n}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=-3,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(-3)=5.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{14}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi (-3)}{6}) \\ 5 & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{14}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot (-1)^{n} \\ \frac{7}{2} & =-\frac{14}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{2n-1} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{2n-1} & =-\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
